statements.text: About 700 agencies surveyed in 43 states. Flock says its technology “supported” about 1 million investigations in 2025, about 20 percent of cleared cases, and helped locate about 10,000 missing people. Flock calls the results “directional estimates rather than audited totals.”
More than 20 billion plate scans a month across the network, according to Flock's website, as reported in November 2025.
More than 100 incidents of license plate reader abuse and misuse, compiled from news reports and records.

excluded.what: Cincinnati calls for service with type LPR, 2018 to 2022: 2,398 calls with coordinates and dispositions including 47 auto-theft recovery reports and 28 calls closed with an arrest
excluded.why: The vendor for that period is not confirmed as Flock; the call type ends in 2022

excluded.what: Minneapolis 911 incidents with the problem type “License Plate Reader”: 208 calls since November 2025, with street-level coordinates and dispositions
excluded.why: The city states its readers are not Flock

excluded.what: Connecticut camera lists from 20 departments obtained by a television station
excluded.why: Locations without outcome counts; not published as data

excluded.what: Minnesota statutory reader logs (times, plates captured, matches by category, fixed locations)
excluded.why: Published per agency behind script-rendered pages; obtainable by records request
